I was CS for a couple years, for a big ol' phone company, so I know how the job goes. It's not rocket science, you're given all the material you need to help just about any customer with just about any issue. There were some real dumb-dumbs in my training class that actually made it through and got onto "the floor," so social skills have just as much to do with it as pulling up Google to find the answer to a particularly tough or confusing question.

But they sure didn't like paying above minimum wage very long! What started out as 'room for advancement' and a decent pay went down to just over the minimum wage with the doors closing a little more every year. This last year the center was shut down, and the only reason I know that is because I drive past it every morning. Something tells me one of the "big four" phone companies didn't just decide to slice their entire CS group by a major chunk because things are working swimmingly nowadays and no one needs the help. I promise you those jobs went overseas.

People wanted those positions, people waited and trained for those positions, and I guarantee you there were some pretty pissed off people when the center closed down.
